missing_experiment_types.name: Acquisition / top-of-funnel / marketing-creative experiments (paid ad creative, SEO/landing pages, app-store listing, install attribution, logged-out/anonymous web)
missing_experiment_types.why_missed: All four lenses are in-product and user-keyed. None has an anonymous/pre-signup visitor entity, so the entire growth-marketing slice of a real roadmap (often 10-20% of experiments) is invisible. A feature store joined on user_id literally cannot represent the cold visitor the experiment targets.

missing_experiment_types.name: Customer support / service / self-serve experiments (chatbot vs human, help-center deflection, refund automation, dispute flows)
missing_experiment_types.why_missed: Support is a large, continuously-experimented surface in any marketplace. Only touched obliquely (trust&safety). The OEC here (contact-rate, CSAT, deflection, refund cost) and its features (ticket history, contact propensity) appear in no lens.

missing_experiment_types.name: Returns / refunds / cancellation-policy & post-purchase experiments (return window, refund friction, order-tracking UX, substitution/out-of-stock handling)
missing_experiment_types.why_missed: HCI names returns only as a distal-inversion risk, never as a first-class experiment type. Grocery/retail/food roadmaps test these constantly; the distal OEC (return rate, refund margin) is exactly where proximal friction signs invert.

missing_experiment_types.name: Privacy / consent / compliance & account-management experiments (consent prompts, ATT, data-export/deletion, age/regulatory gating, dark-pattern remediation)
missing_experiment_types.why_missed: Regulatory-driven roadmap work (DPDP/GDPR/CMA) is real and recurring. Pricing lens flags regulatory backlash as a blind spot but no lens treats consent/compliance UX as an experiment type, and consent-state is never a feature.

missing_experiment_types.name: Internationalization / localization / accessibility experiments (translation quality, RTL, currency/format, a11y modality)
missing_experiment_types.why_missed: HCI carries a11y/locale as context features but no lens has an i18n/a11y experiment type. Direction here is genuinely groundable (a11y reduces friction for affected segments) yet entirely absent.

missing_experiment_types.name: Wallet / stored-value / gift-card / BNPL / payment-method experiments
missing_experiment_types.why_missed: Payment-instrument choice and stored value materially move conversion and retention; covered only as 'payment method count' inside checkout-friction, never as its own type with its own economics (float, breakage, default-instrument).

missing_experiment_types.name: Merchant/seller-as-product-user experiments (merchant dashboard UX, ads-manager, host onboarding funnel, self-serve menu tools)
missing_experiment_types.why_missed: Marketplace/PM lenses treat supply only as economics levers whose outcome lands on the consumer side. The supplier's OWN funnel/UI experiments (a whole B2B product surface) have no experiment type and no supplier-as-user friction/lifecycle features.

missing_experiment_types.name: Content moderation / ranking-safety / integrity-policy experiments (filtering, demotion thresholds, fraud-decline friction)
missing_experiment_types.why_missed: Only verification friction is covered. Threshold experiments that trade false-positive friction against integrity are common and have a distinct OEC (fraud loss vs good-user friction) that none of the feature classes target.

missing_feature_classes.purpose: First-touch acquisition channel, device fingerprint/graph, logged-out session behavior, attribution source. Required to ground any acquisition/landing/logged-out experiment. Every proposed store is user_id-keyed and structurally cannot hold these, leaving the entire top-of-funnel un-addressable.

All four lenses name novelty decay as a blind spot but none proposes the feature class that would mitigate it: per-user exposure age, response-over-time slope, habituation curves, day-1-vs-day-30 deltas. Without a trajectory feature the store is a static snapshot and the durable sign is unrecoverable for the very experiments the lenses admit are novelty-driven.

The standard mitigation for the universally-named LTV/retention blind spot is a validated surrogate index (short-term proxies calibrated against measured long-term outcomes, Netflix/proxy-metric practice). None proposes it, so 'short-run conversion up, LTV down' stays undetectable rather than partially proxied.

Every lens hands aesthetic/relevance/copy direction to 'an LLM layer' but none lists embeddings as a feature class. It is the concrete bridge feature (text/image embedding + LLM-judge score per variant) that would let the empirical store separate within-type creative quality instead of abstaining entirely. Deferring it is defensible; omitting it from the schema is the gap.

PM lens names the ATT/consent instrumentation ceiling as a blind spot, but consent-state and per-user logging coverage are not encoded. They gate whether ALL telemetry-derived classes even exist for a user; without them the engine silently treats missing-because-unconsented as a real-zero and mis-signs the affected segment.

The cross-side spillover class is a per-market aggregate; it cannot support switchback/cluster designs which need graph position, neighbor-treatment exposure, and cluster ids. Since interference is the named killer for the entire two-sided slice, the absence of true network-structure features means those experiment types are listed as 'unlocked' without the features that would actually identify their sign.

PM lens flags that 1000s of concurrent tests interact, but no class encodes which co-running treatments a user is exposed to. Without it, every prior-treatment-response feature is confounded by un-modeled simultaneous arms.

missing_feature_classes.class_name: Assignment-validity features (SRM, exposure-logging integrity, peeking guards)
missing_feature_classes.purpose: The negative-control class guards confounding but not sample-ratio-mismatch, broken exposure logging, or trigger-dilution — the most common reasons a measured sign is an artifact. These are distinct gates from neg-controls and appear nowhere.

hard_or_ungroundable.item: Experiment-history prior store / labeled past-experiment library (the dominant anchor in all four lenses)
hard_or_ungroundable.why: Treated as the single strongest ground for direction, yet it is the hardest asset to actually populate. (1) Company-level cold start: a startup or new surface has near-zero usable history — the very situation where direction help is most wanted. (2) The 'similar treatment on similar surface' match is an unsolved retrieval problem; surface taxonomies drift and metric definitions get redefined (Airbnb Minerva), so labels are not comparable across time. (3) Base rates make the labels noisy: ~1/3 of past experiments are FLAT and ~1/3 negative (Microsoft; Google/Bing only 10-20% positive), so most 'prior signs' are null or underpowered and carry little directional information. The lenses lean on an asset that is itself mostly empty or unreliable.

hard_or_ungroundable.item: Per-user own-price/own-fee elasticity features and per-user CATE/'historical_HTE_decile' uplift features
hard_or_ungroundable.why: These imply quantities that are not identified from observational logs. Price/fee is set by policy, not randomized, so within-user price variation is scarce and confounded with geo/time/context (classic price endogeneity) — per-user elasticity is largely unestimable. Per-user treatment effect is fundamentally unobservable (you never see both potential outcomes for one user); what exists is a model-imputed segment effect, not a measured feature. Schematizing them as populated columns overstates identifiability.

hard_or_ungroundable.item: Friction-telemetry → outcome direction for notification, checkout, and friction-removal types
hard_or_ungroundable.why: HCI grounds the PROXIMAL funnel step, but for exactly these types the proximal sign routinely inverts the OEC: one-click checkout lifts conversion and raises returns/regret; an extra push lifts opens and raises churn/unsub; removing a confirmation cuts effort and raises error/refund/chargeback. Counting these as 'covered' counts the wrong-signed proxy. HCI is honest about the inversion, but the experiment-type coverage table still claims them.

hard_or_ungroundable.item: Two-sided / surge / dispatch / batching direction from market-state features
hard_or_ungroundable.why: All lenses list market-liquidity features as 'unlocking' surge/dispatch/supply-incentive experiment types, while simultaneously naming network interference as a hard blind spot. This is an internal contradiction: market-state features describe the conditioning state but cannot identify the treatment sign from per-user randomized data — that requires switchback/cluster designs the feature store does not provide. The sign is not groundable observationally regardless of how rich the market features are.

hard_or_ungroundable.item: Negative-control guard as a correctness mechanism
hard_or_ungroundable.why: Marketplace lens is honest ('buys abstention, not correctness'), but the broader reliance assumes a negative control that is actually coupled to the latent confounder. The team's own work notes the guard 'needs strongly-coupled NC (LLM picks it)' and flagged 0/3 errors before the guard existed; NC coverage of the relevant confounder is not guaranteed, so abstention itself is only partial.

Mostly true but overstated as universal: documented non-monotone cases exist (too-fast renders read as untrustworthy or skip perceived effort; faster surfacing can increase choice overload). Direction is high-confidence but not a free win, and magnitude/segment varies more than the 'best-grounded type' framing implies.

merges: The four experiment-history assets are ONE store at different grains, not four classes: marketplace 'Experiment-history prior store' (surface×family×metric), PM 'Prior treatment-response meta-features' (segment×family), pricing 'Past-treatment-response priors' (user×family), HCI 'Labeled past-UI-experiment library' (experiment×arm×segment). Merge into a single multi-grain experiment-history store — the largest redundancy in the council.

RFM / engagement / habit / tenure appears in all four (marketplace 'User engagement state', PM 'Engagement frequency & recency', pricing 'Engagement/habit/RFM state', HCI 'User proficiency/tenure'). Collapse to one Lifecycle+RFM+habit class.

Price sensitivity is fragmented: pricing lens alone splits it into four (own-price elasticity, reference-price/anchoring, deal-proneness, WTP) while marketplace and PM each have a single 'elasticity' class. Consolidate to elasticity + anchoring/reference + deal-proneness, then dedup against the other two lenses.

Funnel/session/friction telemetry is duplicated four ways (marketplace 'Session funnel telemetry', PM 'Funnel step conversion', pricing 'Funnel friction & session', HCI 'Per-surface friction' + 'Funnel/flow step'). Merge into one friction/funnel telemetry family using HCI's more granular event schema.
Notification responsiveness & fatigue is near-identical in marketplace, PM, and pricing — merge to one channel-responsiveness+fatigue class.
Device/platform/context appears in marketplace, PM, and HCI — merge to one.
Market supply/demand balance appears in marketplace, PM, and pricing — merge to one market-state class.
Merchant/item quality is split inconsistently (item-grain vs merchant-grain vs 'surface-content') across all four — normalize to two entity classes: per-item and per-merchant.

Churn-risk/LTV/value-segment (marketplace 'User value & churn-risk') and lifecycle/churn (pricing) overlap with the RFM merge and with subscription-state (PM 'Loyalty/subscription' + pricing 'Subscription/membership') — consolidate value/churn/membership into one monetization-state class.
Trust/social-proof sensitivity (PM and pricing) and default-acceptance/cognitive-load (pricing 'Default-acceptance', PM 'Friction/cognitive-load') each appear twice — merge each pair.

Affinity/preference embeddings (marketplace + PM) overlap with pricing 'Substitution & choice-set' — merge into one preference/substitution class. Net: the ~67 listed classes across the four lenses reduce to ~22-25 distinct classes (~60% redundancy).
roadmap_coverage_estimate: Honest union coverage for DIRECTION prediction: ~35-45% of a real consumer-marketplace roadmap at usefully-better-than-chance, and only ~10-20% on the decision-relevant counter-intuitive subset. Derivation: (a) ~1/3 of experiments are statistically FLAT and another large share underpowered (Microsoft 1/3 positive / 1/3 flat / 1/3 negative; Google/Bing 10-20% positive) — for the flat/tiny third 'direction' is ill-posed, capping any predictor. (b) Of the genuinely-non-null remainder, the union grounds: UI/copy/flow/onboarding (~40-55% of roadmap volume) but only ~half of that is friction-expressible rather than aesthetic/relevance ties, and a slice of those have proximal→distal inversion → net ~50-60% of UI work; pricing/promo (~15-20%) only where the lever historically varied and is not interference-dominated → ~50%; ranking/recs (~10-15%) reduced by relevance ties and offline-online gap → ~50%; notification/lifecycle (~5-10%) proximal-yes/distal-no → ~50%; supply-side/equilibrium/dispatch (~5-10%) → ~15% (needs switchback, not a feature store); net-new/brand (~5%) → ~0%. (c) Entirely-missing roadmap slices none of the lenses addressed — acquisition/marketing, support/service, returns/refunds, privacy/compliance, merchant-as-user — are ~10-15% of a real org's roadmap at 0% coverage. (d) The strongest anchor (experiment-history prior) is unpopulated at company cold-start, so for a NEW org real coverage drops toward the low end (~25-30%). Residual un-groundable ~55-65%, dominated by: aesthetic/relevance ties; proximal→distal sign inversion; novelty decay and long-horizon retention (no longitudinal/surrogate features); two-sided interference (wrong experimental design, not a feature gap); cold-start net-new surfaces; the missing roadmap slices; and counter-intuitive cross-segment trade-down — the engine 'tracks intuition not truth' (the team's own blind tests: 0-for-1 on counter-intuitive cases), so coverage is LOWEST exactly where a direction-predictor would be most valuable. The average ~40% figure materially overstates decision-relevant value; the council should report the counter-intuitive-subset number (~10-20%) as the honest product ceiling and design for abstention + external-validity auditing rather than blanket prediction. This matches the existing internal finding that the causal/uplift route works only for the feature-expressible slice (a router, not an LLM replacement).
